This is the second bail application.
The first bail application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to the learned counsel to file a fresh bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State, and perused the record.

This bail application has been filed seeking release of accused/applicant Manoj Kumar Pandey for grant of bail, who is involved in Case Crime No. 244 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C.and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Nasirabad, District Raebareli.
The first bail application was dismissed as not pressed by the order of Hon'ble Justice Mr. Shamim Ahmed vide order dated 02.09.2022 in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 3408 of 2021.

Learned counsel for the applicant also submitted that the applicant was not present at the place of occurrence, rather the incident took place at the house of his sister which is far away from the village of the applicant.
It is further submitted that the marriage had taken place prior to four years and no F.I.R. for dowry demand or harassment was ever lodged by the family members of the deceased.
The applicant has been falsely implicated in this case only for the reason that the applicant is the husband of the deceased.
There is no direct evidence found against the applicant for incriminating him for the commission of the said crime.
There is no criminal history against the applicant and he is languishing in jail since 07.09.2020.

Learned A.G.A. has, however, opposed the prayer for grant of bail and has submitted that it is a case of 304-B I.P.C. and the deceased committed suicide because of the torture meted out to her by her husband and her in-laws thus, the applicant does not deserve mercy of the Court and his bail application is liable to be rejected.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, perusing the record, considering the nature of allegations, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, particularly the fact that at the time of death of the deceased, she was present in the house of her sister-in-law (nanad) and there she consumed poison for which the applicant prima facie may not be held responsible, I find it to be a fit case for grant of bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.

Let the accused/applicant Manoj Kumar Pandey involved in above-mentioned case be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not communicate with any of the prosecution witness including the informant and the violation of this condition alone shall be a sufficient ground for the trial court to cancel the facility of bail granted to the applicant.
(ii) Applicant shall not take adjournment on any of the date on which the prosecution witness(s) are in attendance and in this regard shall file an undertaking before the trial court.

(iii) If in case of any exigency/urgency the applicant is not able to appear before the trial court he shall instruct his counsel engaged in the trial court to do all required for early disposal of the case including the cross examination of any prosecution witness.
(iv) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
